story.titleZh: 安东内利承认巴库Q1撞墙是“不必要的失误”
story.summaryZh: 世界冠军领跑者基米·安东内利在阿塞拜疆大奖赛排位赛Q1撞墙，将从第16位发车，他称对此“非常恼火”，并承认是自己的“不必要”失误。队友乔治·拉塞尔夺得杆位，并表示不能把安东内利排除在争冠行列之外。
story.originalTitle: 'I'm very mad about it' - Antonelli admits to 'unnecessary mistake'
detailZh: 基米·安东内利对阿塞拜疆大奖赛排位赛撞车“非常恼火”，乔治·拉塞尔拒绝将队友排除在争胜行列之外
基米·安东内利在阿塞拜疆排位赛第一阶段撞车，将从第16位发车；乔治·拉塞尔夺得杆位，展现了梅赛德斯的强劲速度；周六中午12点（预热节目上午10点30分开始）在天空体育 F1和Main Event观看阿塞拜疆大奖赛直播
基米·安东内利在阿塞拜疆大奖赛排位赛中撞墙
世界冠军领跑者基米·安东内利表示，他对导致自己从阿塞拜疆大奖赛第16位发车的“不必要”排位赛失误感到“非常恼火”。
安东内利在赛季还剩九场比赛时以81分领跑积分榜，这一优势让他处于只要取得稳定成绩就能赢得首个世界冠军的位置。
正因如此，再加上他本赛季迄今展现出的统治级状态，当安东内利在巴库Q1第一弯擦到护墙时，这令人极为意外，尤其是考虑到梅赛德斯当时展现出强劲速度，本应让他轻松晋级Q3。

梅赛德斯在这条赛道上的实力体现在安东内利的队友——也是他最接近的争冠对手——乔治·拉塞尔以超过0.8秒的优势击败法拉利的查尔斯·勒克莱尔夺得杆位。
梅赛德斯的安东内利在阿塞拜疆大奖赛因一次“不必要”的撞车提前结束排位赛后感到沮丧
当被问及是否因为第一弯抓地力比他预想的更多而措手不及时，安东内利告诉天空体育 F1：“是的，当然。抓地力一圈比一圈提升得很快。”
“突然我转向时，前部抓地力比上一圈多得多，然后我碰到了墙。”
“所以，是我的失误。非常不必要。说实话，我对此非常恼火，明天会努力做得更好。”
“过去的基米”的“不可思议的失误”
前世界冠军雅克·维伦纽夫将这一事件描述为“不可思议的失误”。
“这不是一英寸的问题，而是很多，”天空体育 F1的维伦纽夫说。“不可思议的失误，而且他是在队友独一档的周末犯下这个错误。”
“这个时机不太好，但按照现行规则，他们更容易从后方追回来。”
2026年阿塞拜疆大奖赛排位赛集锦
三届W系列赛冠军杰米·查德威克表示，这次撞车让她想起“过去的基米”，指的是这位20岁车手在F1首个赛季表现不稳定，曾引发人们对他能否兑现一代天才声誉的重大质疑。
天空体育 F1的查德威克说：“我说这很不寻常，我们经常看到基米开车的方式就是只有一个挡位。全速前进。全力以赴。”
“去年我们看到这带来了失误和撞车，今年我们在他身上基本没看到这种情况。感觉有点像过去的基米，就是那种只有一个挡位，而他其实并不需要那样做。”
“话虽如此，在这样的赛道上，我们知道很容易犯这种错误。但你开的是一辆在这条赛道上明显独一档的梅赛德斯，Q1第一圈，你不需要冒那么大风险。”
“只是第一弯的抓地力让他措手不及。他转向时，进入排位赛，赛车总是比FP3时更有活力一些，这让他措手不及。”
拉塞尔“不能排除”安东内利争胜
周六的比赛距离安东内利在意大利大奖赛的惊艳胜利仅三周，那场比赛他从第19位发车，最终赢下主场之战。
在蒙扎从第二位发车并一度领先、随后被安东内利超越的拉塞尔，对队友在巴库从后方发车可能构成的威胁保持警惕。
“显然，你不能排除基米，”拉塞尔说。“他在蒙扎从第19位发车，现在他在第16位，所以这次他应该能提前几圈领跑。”
拉塞尔被问及是否认为安东内利在接近首个冠军时出现“紧张”，但他指出，即使在夺冠赛季，车手也往往会犯错。
天空体育 F1的卡伦·钱多克与乔治·拉塞尔一起回看他在阿塞拜疆大奖赛的杆位圈
这位英国人更愿意专注于自己在巴库迄今的强劲表现，即使在Q1撞车之前，他似乎也对比安东内利占据优势。
“我想不起来他本赛季犯过多少错误，”拉塞尔说。“我们今天这边的表现很棒，但他整个赛季都无懈可击。”
“当你回顾每一个冠军赛季，即使是最终获胜者，过程中也会有失误。”
“我仍然继续相信、继续战斗，直到不再可能为止，但我没有感到任何压力。现在每次坐进车里我都感到兴奋，纯粹是因为我对自己更有信心。”
“当这种信心开始建立时，就像是一个向上的循环。反过来，当你处于被动时，你开始失去信心，然后你开始更多地挑战极限，那正是失误发生的时候。”
detailEn: Kimi Antonelli 'very mad' about Azerbaijan GP qualifying crash as George Russell refuses to discount team-mate from battle for win

Kimi Antonelli crashed in the first part of qualifying in Azerbaijan, leaving him 16th on the grid; George Russell exhibited Mercedes' strong pace by taking pole; watch the Azerbaijan GP on Saturday at 12pm with build-up from 10.30am, live on Sky Sports F1 and Main Event
Kimi Antonelli hits the wall during qualifying at the Azerbaijan GP
World championship leader Kimi Antonelli said he was "very mad" about making an "unnecessary" qualifying error that left him starting the Azerbaijan Grand Prix from 16th on the grid.
The 81-point lead established by Antonelli at the top of the standings with nine races remaining has put him in a position where merely solid results will see the Italian to a maiden title.

For that reason, along with the imperious form he has shown throughout the season so far, it came as a major surprise when Antonelli clipped the wall at the first corner during Q1 in Baku, especially given Mercedes were showing strong pace that should have enabled him to cruise through to Q3 at a canter.

The Silver Arrows' strength at the circuit was evidenced in Antonelli's team-mate - and nearest title challenger - George Russell beating Ferrari's Charles Leclerc to pole by more than eight tenths of a second.
Mercedes' Antonelli was left frustrated after an 'unnecessary' crash which ended his qualifying early at the Azerbaijan GP
Asked whether he had been caught out by there being more grip than he expected at the first corner, Antonelli told Sky Sports F1: "Yeah, for sure. The grip was coming up very quickly lap by lap.
"Suddenly I turned in and had a lot more front end compared to the lap before and I touched the wall.
"So, mistake from my side. Very unnecessary. To be fair, I'm very mad about it and will try to do better tomorrow."
'An incredible mistake' from 'the Kimi of old'
Former world champion Jacques Villeneuve described the incident as "an incredible mistake".
"It's not an inch, it's a lot," Sky Sports F1's Villeneuve said. "An incredible mistake and he does it on a weekend where his team-mate is in a league of his own.
"Not the best of time for that, but with the current rules they facilitate getting back through the field."
Highlights from qualifying for the 2026 Azerbaijan Grand Prix

Three-time W series champion Jamie Chadwick said the crash reminded her of "Kimi of old", a reference to the 20-year-old's inconsistent debut campaign in F1, which raised major doubts over whether he could live up to his billing as a generational talent.
Sky Sports F1's Chadwick said: "I say it's uncharacteristic, it's kind of the way we see Kimi drive a lot of the time is that there's one gear. It's all in. It's all everything.

"Last year we saw that come with mistakes and crashes, this year we have not really seen that of him. It has felt a bit like Kimi of old in a way and it was like that one gear and he just didn't really need to do it.

"That said, it is easy to make mistakes like that, we know that at a track like this. But you are in a Mercedes that was clearly in a league of his own at this track, first lap of Q1, you didn't need to take that much risk.

"It just caught him out, the grip that he clearly had at Turn One. He turned in, you go into qualifying and the car is always a bit more alive I guess than it would have been for him in FP3 and it has caught him out."
Russell 'can't discount' Antonelli from battle for win
Saturday's race comes just three weeks on from Antonelli's stunning victory at the Italian Grand Prix, which saw him come from 19th on the grid to win his home race.
Russell, who started second in Monza and led before being overhauled by Antonelli, is wary of the threat his team-mate could pose from towards the back of the grid in Baku.
"Obviously, you can't discount Kimi," Russell said. "He started 19th in Monza and now he's in 16th, so he should be leading by a few laps earlier this time."
Russell was asked whether he thought Antonelli was experiencing "jitters" as he nears a fist title, but pointed out that even in championship-winning campaigns, drivers tend to make mistakes.
Sky Sports F1's Karun Chandhok is joined by George Russell to watch back his pole-setting lap for the Azerbaijan GP
The Brit preferred to focus on his own strong performance so far in Baku, which had seen him appear to have an edge over Antonelli even before the Q1 crash.
"I can't recall many mistakes he's made this season," Russell said. "The performance our side today was great, but he's been flawless this whole season.
"When you look at every championship campaign, even for the winners, there are mistakes along the way.

"I still keep on believing and keep on fighting until it isn't possible anymore, but I don't feel any pressure. I feel excitement every time I jump in the car now, purely because I feel more confident in myself.

"When that confidence starts to build, it's just like this upward cycle. And on the flip side, when you're on the back foot, you start losing that confidence, and then you start pushing the limits more, and that's when mistakes happen.

detailZh: 刘易斯·汉密尔顿：法拉利车队的七届F1世界冠军在访问拉法口岸后，呼吁以色列“放行援助卡车”进入加沙。
刘易斯·汉密尔顿周二访问了拉法口岸，实地了解向加沙运送援助物资的工作；这位法拉利车手周三在Instagram发帖，呼吁以色列“履行停火协议下的义务”。
刘易斯·汉密尔顿在访问拉法口岸后，呼吁以色列“放行援助卡车”进入加沙。
汉密尔顿周二在埃及，实地了解向加沙运送人道主义与救援物资的工作。这位法拉利车手还参观了拉法口岸，并走访了埃及红新月会的援助仓库。
美国支持的以色列与哈马斯之间的停火协议仍然有效，但并未结束以色列对加沙的打击，同时联合国世界粮食计划署表示，加沙三分之二的人口难以获得足够的食物。
汉密尔顿此前曾呼吁该地区实现和平，他表示援助物资因“疯狂的理由”被拒绝进入加沙。
刘易斯·汉密尔顿（@lewishamilton）分享的一条帖子。
您可以随时通过隐私选项更改您的设置。
这位七届世界冠军在Instagram上发文称：“过去三年以色列在加沙的种族灭绝行径令人震惊。”
“人们被剥夺自由、安全和尊严，这是不公正的。任何人都不应被当作生命不那么重要来对待。”
“我看到绵延数英里的围墙，是为了把他们困在里面而建的。站在外面，感觉就像一座露天监狱，我满脑子想的都是进去帮忙。”
“在拉法口岸，我看到食品卡车排着队准备出发，但它们经常不被允许进入，或者面临严重延误。我交谈过的排在第一位的那位司机已经等了超过12个小时。”
在附近的物流中心，我看到了救援人员的辛勤工作，但我也看到了因荒唐理由被拒绝的物资。睡袋、急救包、医疗设备、轮椅，甚至给孩子们的足球。
以色列需要履行停火协议下的义务，让援助卡车进入。没有任何借口。
我知道很多人都感受到同样的无助。同样觉得需要做点什么，而不是袖手旁观。我不想让我们对他们的苦难习以为常。我不想让我们移开视线。
周三，以色列总理本雅明·内塔尼亚胡否认以色列在拖延物资进入加沙，并将加沙不断恶化的状况归咎于哈马斯，指责他们拒绝解除武装并截留援助物资用于军事用途。
2021年，汉密尔顿创立了Mission 44慈善机构，旨在支持年轻人并改善他们获得教育和就业机会的途径。
他还支持了人道主义和救援倡议，以及为受冲突影响的人们提供帮助的努力。
汉密尔顿是在上周末参加圣保罗大奖赛并获得第九名后进行了此次访问。他接下来将代表法拉利参加拉斯维加斯大奖赛，第一次练习赛于11月20日星期五举行。
汉密尔顿分享了与加沙儿童会面的细节
在首次发帖一天后，汉密尔顿于周四再次通过社交媒体分享了他与从加沙撤离的儿童互动的细节。
除了分享一组自己与孩子们的合影外，汉密尔顿写道：“在埃及见到一些由@inaraorg支持的从加沙撤离的巴勒斯坦儿童，我的心都碎了。
“这些美丽、聪明的孩子经历了创伤、悲痛和可怕的伤害，这些是任何孩子都不应该承受的事情。有些孩子在袭击中中弹或严重烧伤，仍在面对复杂的康复之路。但真正打动我的是他们如此坚韧，而且似乎在彼此身上找到了许多快乐。
刘易斯·汉密尔顿（@lewishamilton）分享的帖子

“当我问起他们的梦想时，他们谈到想成为老师和医生，这样就能像曾经帮助过他们的人那样去帮助别人。在经历了这一切之后，他们仍然想象着一个关爱他人的未来。这让我一直难以忘怀。
“我在学校、医院和一家心理健康诊所遇到了孩子们，帮助他们走出创伤。我还走进了一些家庭，倾听他们关于康复以及与亲人——他们的孩子、父母、兄弟姐妹——分离的故事。那种分离和不确定带来的痛苦令人难以理解。
“他们的故事让我想到了仍留在加沙的孩子们，他们生活在恶劣的条件下。据报道，自2023年10月以来，已有超过21500名儿童丧生，45000人受伤。他们每一个人都曾有过一个家和一个未来。我们不能忘记他们。
“这些孩子和你们的孩子没有不同。他们的生命同样珍贵。他们本应能在教室里与朋友相伴感到安全，与家人在一起，并憧憬未来。我非常感激我遇到的年轻人正在获得他们所需的帮助，但他们不得不离开家园去寻找安全，这令人心碎。”
加沙卫生当局表示，自2023年10月以色列开始对加沙发动攻势以来，已有超过74000人丧生。

detailEn: Lewis Hamilton: Ferrari's seven-time F1 world champion urges Israel to 'let the aid trucks in' to Gaza after visit to Rafah border

Lewis Hamilton visited the Rafah border on Tuesday to witness efforts to transport aid into Gaza; Ferrari driver published Instagram post on Wednesday calling on Israel to "fulfil its obligations under the ceasefire"
Lewis Hamilton urged Israel to "let the aid trucks in" to Gaza after visiting the Rafah border.

Hamilton was in Egypt on Tuesday to witness efforts to deliver humanitarian and relief aid bound for Gaza. The Ferrari driver also toured the Rafah border crossing and visited the Egyptian Red Crescent's aid warehouses.

The US-backed ceasefire between Israel and Hamas remains in place but has not ended Israeli strikes on Gaza, while the UN World Food Programme says two-thirds of Gaza's population are struggling to get enough to eat.
Hamilton - who has previously called for peace in the region - said aid was being denied entry into Gaza for "crazy reasons".

The seven-time world champion posted on Instagram: "The past three years of Israel's genocide in Gaza is appalling.
"It's an injustice for people to be denied their freedom, their safety and their dignity. No human being should be treated as though their life matters less.
"I saw walls stretching for miles, built to keep them in. Standing there, outside what felt like an open-air prison, all I could think about was getting in to help.
"At Rafah border, I saw food trucks lined up ready to go, but they're regularly not allowed in or face major delays. The first driver in line that I spoke to had already been waiting over 12 hours.

"At the nearby logistics centre, I saw the hard work of the aid workers, but I also saw what gets rejected for crazy reasons. Sleeping bags, first-aid kits, medical equipment, wheelchairs, even footballs for kids.
"Israel needs to fulfil its obligations under the ceasefire and let the aid trucks in. No excuse.
"I know so many people feel that same helplessness. That same need to do something rather than just watch. I don't want us to get used to their suffering. I don't want us to look away."

On Wednesday, Benjamin Netanyahu, the Israeli Prime Minister, denied Israel was delaying the entry of supplies into Gaza, and blamed Hamas for the worsening conditions in Gaza, accusing them of a refusal to disarm and seizing aid for military use.
In 2021, Hamilton founded Mission 44, a charity aimed at supporting young people and improving ⁠access to education and employment ​opportunities.
He has also backed ​humanitarian and relief initiatives, and ​efforts to support people affected by ⁠conflict.
Hamilton made his visit after competing in the Sao Paulo GP last weekend, where he finished ninth. He will next compete for Ferrari in the Las Vegas GP, with Practice 1 on Friday November 20.
Hamilton shares details of meeting children from Gaza
A day after his initial post, Hamilton took to social media again on Thursday to share details of his interactions with children he met who have been evacuated from Gaza.

Along with sharing a selection of photos of himself with the children, Hamilton wrote: "Meeting some of the Palestinian children evacuated from Gaza and supported by @inaraorg in Egypt broke my heart.

"Beautiful, bright children who have faced trauma, grief and horrendous injuries, things no child should ever have to endure. Some have been shot or badly burned in attacks and are still facing a complicated road towards recovery. But what really struck me was how resilient they were and how much joy they seem to find in each other.

"When I asked about their dreams, they spoke about becoming teachers and doctors so they could help others, the way they were helped. After everything they've been through, they still imagine a future caring for other people. That has stayed with me.

"I met children at school, in hospital and at a mental health clinic helping them work through their trauma. I also went into families' homes and listened to their stories of recovery and being separated from loved ones - their children, their parents, their siblings. The pain of that separation and uncertainty is hard to comprehend.

"Their stories made me think about the children still in Gaza, who are living in terrible conditions. According to reports, more than 21,500 children have been killed and 45,000 injured since October 2023. Every one of them had a home and a future. We can't forget them.

"These children are no different from yours. Their lives are just as precious. They should be able to feel safe in a classroom with friends, be with their families and imagine a future. I'm so grateful the young people I met are getting the help they need, but it's heartbreaking that they've had to leave their homes to find safety."
Gaza health authorities say more than 74,000 people have been killed since Israel began its Gaza assault in October 2023.
Israel launched the offensive after Hamas gunmen led an attack on southern Israel, which it said killed around 1,200.
